sections.preface: Outlines the full experimental program E0-E9 and the parallel ablation matrix A0-A9 used to test graph mask, typing, uncertainty, singularity, and IDF mechanisms.
Details ablations E4 through E7, covering singularity-detector AUROC, IDF weighting, group-quotient attention, and reservoir-readout efficiency.
Reports a proof-of-concept MNIST experiment combining typed states with confusion-graph singularity detection.
Motivates the choice of BabyAI as the testbed for hierarchical task and state-machine evaluation due to its compositional instruction grammar.
Presents synthetic BabyAI-like grid results, where the graph mask and typed features yield substantial accuracy gains except when the classifier already observes current-state identity.
